chunks: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'My father narrated to me that the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family)
judged with a witness and an oath.'

key_terms.شَاهِد: A single witness (shahid); one of the standard evidential requirements in Islamic jurisprudence
key_terms.قَضَى: Judged/ruled (qada); refers to a formal legal judgment of the Prophet acting as head of state and judge
key_terms.يَمِين: Oath (yamin); the sworn affirmation by the claimant that supplements one witness to constitute full proof

ai.seo_question: Did the Prophet judge with one witness and an oath in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) transmits from his father Imam al-Baqir (AS) a ruling of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) that a legal judgment may be rendered based on a single witness combined with the oath of the plaintiff. This hadith establishes a key principle of Shia Islamic judicial procedure: when a claimant produces one witness but lacks two, the court may accept the single witness together with the claimant's sworn oath as sufficient evidence. The original audience — early Shia jurists — would have understood this as a binding prophetic precedent applicable to financial and civil disputes.
